Prospective clinical trials are preferred, but multi-institutional retrospective case series will also be strongly considered. Research projects can include, but are not limited to, the study of new surgical techniques, multimodality treatment protocols, novel adjuvant agents, and treatment outcomes for different tumor types. Research Proposal Submission Requests for more information and proposal submissions can be directed to Dr. Brandan Janssens or Dr. Mirja Nolff, the VSSO Research Committee, by clicking on the link below. Research Proposal Guideline Form Contact research committee Submit a proposal DATA collection spreadsheet template OPEN RESEARCH TRIALS JUNE 2026 Evaluation of incidence and risk factors for surgical site infection following neoplastic canine limb amputations performed with and without a bipolar sealing device Lead investigator: Andrea Erickson, DVM, DACVS-SA, ACVS Fellow – Surgical Oncology, EDUCT-MA (BME), Assistant Professor – Surgical Oncology and Soft Tissue Surgery, Oregon State University Aim and objectives: The aim of this study is to evaluate the incidence and risk factors for surgical site infection (SSI) following neoplastic limb amputations performed with and without a bipolar vessel sealing device. Furthermore, we want to evaluate the influence of anesthetic and surgical time on SSI incidence for neoplastic limb amputations. Please contact Dr. Erickson for more details. OCTOBER 2025 Retrospective evaluation of impact of lymphadenectomy on survival of dogs with cutaneous mast cell tumors. Lead investigator: Dr. Mirja Nolff (Clinic of Small Animal Surgery, Vetsuisse Zürich, University of Zürich, Switzerland). Aim and objectives: The aim of this study is, to assess the impact of nodal management on outcome in dogs with grade 2/low grade mast cell tumors that are solely treated by surgical intervention. Furthermore, we want to assess if SLN based resection results in a superior outcome compared to regional lymphadenectomy. Our hypothesis is, that lymphadenectomy will result in improved survival time compared to cases were lymph-nodes were not treated in both species. Furthermore, we propose that this effect will be more pronounced in dogs when SLN mapping was used to determine the nodes to be resected. Please contact Dr. Nolff for more details. 2022 The effects of lymph node extirpation on long-term prognosis of non-metastatic canine oral malignant melanoma. Lead investigator: Dr. Judith Bertran Aims and objectives of the study: To compare the disease progression rates, survival times of two treatment groups of nonmetastatic canine oral malignant melanoma (Stage I and Stage II with N0)— (1) primary tumor/local surgical excision (group 1) versus (2) primary tumor removal with non-selective cervical LNs extirpation (group 2).
